values: An inactive user account must not be permitted to access ColdChainX operations.
A customer who registers independently must be assigned the Customer role.
Only an administrator may create a driver account.
Administrative users are entitled to all active business permissions.
A user-specific permission decision must take precedence over the permission inherited from the user's role, and an explicit denial must prevent the affected action.
An operational assignment may only be issued to an active employee who belongs to the relevant warehouse and holds the permission required for the work.
An employee must not have more than one active assignment for the same business reference.
Only the assigned employee may start or complete an assignment, and the employee must retain the required permission when doing so.
A manager may cancel an assignment only before the assignment is completed or already cancelled.
Sales personnel are responsible for reviewing customer orders, issuing quotations, and administering commercial contracts.
Dispatch personnel are responsible for trip planning, transport allocation, and active-delivery oversight.
Authorized warehouse personnel are responsible for receiving, quality inspection, putaway, picking, loading, and return processing.
Accounting personnel are responsible for financial review, reimbursement, claims payout, and invoice control.
A customer may access or act only on the customer's own orders, quotations, contracts, advance shipping notices, and invoices.
Order conversations may involve only the order's customer and authorized Sales, Warehouse, or Administrative personnel.
A customer may create an advance shipping notice only for the customer's own order after the order contract has been signed.
An advance shipping notice must identify a valid receiving warehouse and request a drop-off time at least six hours after the notice is created.
A newly accepted advance shipping notice must enter the Scheduled state pending warehouse receipt.
Every order must be classified as Meat and Seafood, Frozen Fruit and Vegetables, Ice Cream and Beverages, Pharmaceuticals, or Raw Materials and Other Goods.
The required storage temperature declared for an order must be between -18°C and -5°C, inclusive.
Cargo must use an approved handling unit: pallet, crate, sack, plastic box, foam box, or carton box.
Cargo quantities, weights, and dimensions used for storage and transport planning must be positive values.
LPNs combined within the same transport load must belong to the same product category.
The permitted temperature tolerance for a combined load must be the strictest applicable tolerance: 0°C for pharmaceuticals, 1°C for ice cream and beverages, and 2°C for other supported categories.
Strong-odor cargo must not be combined with ice cream or beverage cargo.
A cold warehouse must define a minimum and maximum operating temperature, and the maximum must be higher than the minimum.
Temperature ranges must not be assigned to warehouses that are not designated for cold storage.
Warehouse capacity must be maintained as a non-negative operational limit.

Inventory ageing must be classified as Red when an LPN has remained in stock for more than 48 hours or has fewer than 12 hours before its service deadline, Yellow when it has remained for more than 24 hours, and Green otherwise.
A warehouse temperature audit must identify any LPN whose required temperature falls outside the warehouse's approved operating range.
An LPN may be withdrawn from warehouse records only while it is Expected, In Stock, on Discrepancy Hold, or Pending Return; an LPN already committed to outbound movement must remain traceable.
An order may be booked only against an active schedule and before that schedule's Vietnam-local booking cutoff.
A newly created order must enter Pending Review and must have a Draft quotation prepared for commercial review.
A customer may amend or withdraw an order only while it is Pending Review or Needs Update.
A customer resubmitting an order that Needs Update must return the order to Pending Review.
Sales personnel may review an order only while it is Pending Review.
A request for customer correction must include a customer-facing explanation and must place the order in Needs Update.
A compliance rejection must include a customer-facing reason and must place the order in Rejected.
Sales personnel may approve an order only when its quotation is still in Draft, after which the order must enter Approved.
Order volume must be calculated from the cargo dimensions and quantity and expressed in cubic metres.
Chargeable weight must be the greatest of actual or expected weight, volumetric weight, and the 30-kilogram minimum charge.
Base freight must be calculated from the chargeable weight and the applicable route weight tier.
Last-mile charges must be calculated from the delivery distance and the applicable per-kilometre rate.
Unless another approved rate applies, order charges must include value-added tax at 8 percent.
A quotation may be commercially revised only while it is in Draft.
Sending a Draft quotation to the customer must place the quotation in Sent and the order in Quoting.
Only the owning customer may accept a Sent quotation; acceptance must place the quotation in Accepted and the order in Contract Pending.
A customer may add only active, non-mandatory value-added services to an order, and the contract value must be recalculated accordingly.
A contract may be created only from an Accepted quotation and must not duplicate another contract awaiting signature for the same order.
A commercial contract must expire one year after its effective creation date.
A contract may be revised only while it is in Draft or Pending Signature.
Sending a contract for signature must place it in Pending Customer Signature.
Only the owning customer may submit the signed contract, after which the contract must enter Pending Sales Verification.
Sales personnel returning a signed contract for correction must provide a customer-facing reason and return it to Pending Customer Signature.
Sales verification of a signed contract must activate the contract, place the order in Contract Signed, assign a unique tracking identity, and require the commercial delivery documents.
An order must not have more than one active commercial appendix in Draft or Sent at the same time.
When actual received measurements differ from the contracted measurements, the appendix price must be based on the actual measurements and show the difference from the original base charge.
Only Sales personnel may send or execute a commercial appendix, and only the owning customer may accept or reject a Sent appendix.
Executing an accepted appendix must release the affected LPN for receiving and create an adjustment invoice for the price difference plus 8 percent value-added tax, due within 15 days.
Executing a rejected appendix must place the affected LPN and order in Return Pending, apply a return penalty of VND 200,000, and issue a return slip.
Inbound quality inspection may begin only for an LPN covered by a valid advance shipping notice assigned to the receiving warehouse.
Inbound inspection must compare actual weight and volume with the expected values; a variance greater than 5 percent in either measure constitutes a discrepancy.
An LPN that passes inbound inspection must enter Receiving, the advance shipping notice must enter QC Passed, the order must enter Receiving, and the receipt must await putaway.
A material inbound discrepancy must place the LPN, advance shipping notice, and order on Discrepancy Hold and must produce a discrepancy report and Draft commercial appendix.
An LPN on Discrepancy Hold may be released to Receiving only after reevaluation confirms that its weight and volume variances are within the 5 percent tolerance.
An LPN batch must not have a future manufacturing date, and its expiry date must be later than both the manufacturing date and the receiving date.
Each received LPN must have a 24-hour service deadline for completion of its inbound processing.
Putaway may occur only after an LPN has passed into Receiving and has been assigned a storage location; successful putaway must place the LPN and order In Stock.
A returned LPN may re-enter stock only from Return Pending or Delivery Returned.
When every LPN in an order has been returned to the hub, the order must enter Returned to Hub.
A return document may be issued only for an LPN in Return Pending and only after at least one applicable penalty charge has been paid.
All LPNs assigned to one trip must belong to the same active schedule and origin warehouse.
An LPN may be allocated to a trip only when it is In Stock, is not assigned to another active trip, and has a declared temperature requirement.
A vehicle may be assigned only when it is Active, located at the trip origin, and capable of maintaining the required temperature range for every allocated LPN.
Every allocated LPN must fit within the vehicle's usable dimensions, and the total load must remain within the vehicle's weight and spatial capacity.
A trip must be assigned one or two eligible drivers; when two are assigned, one must be Primary and the other Secondary.
A driver may be assigned only when Active or Available, located at the trip origin, and holding a current, unexpired driving licence.
A vehicle or driver must not be allocated to more than one active trip at the same time.
Planned driver duty must not exceed 10 hours in a day or 48 hours in a week; a driver who exceeds either limit must enter mandatory rest.
Creating a trip must place the trip in Planned, reserve its LPNs as Allocated, place the affected orders in Loading, and reserve the assigned vehicle and drivers for planning.
Picking may start only for a Planned trip and must move each selected LPN from Allocated to Loading.
Loading may be completed only when every trip LPN is in Loading; completion must release the LPNs for dispatch and place the trip in Loading Completed.
A trip may be sealed and dispatched only after loading is complete, all LPNs are released, and all assigned drivers remain eligible.
Dispatch must place the trip In Transit, place its LPNs in Shipping, and place the assigned vehicle and drivers On Trip.
A trip must not be cancelled after any of its LPNs has entered Shipping.
Cancelling an eligible pre-dispatch trip must return its LPNs and affected orders to In Stock and release all reserved vehicles, drivers, seals, and delivery stops.
A vehicle's registration plate, chassis number, and engine number must each uniquely identify a non-retired fleet asset.
A vehicle's declared carrying capacity and usable dimensions must be positive, and its declared maximum volume must not exceed its physical cargo-space volume.
A refrigerated vehicle's maximum operating temperature must not be lower than its minimum operating temperature.
A fleet vehicle must hold current registration, insurance, and city permits; a vehicle with missing or expired mandatory documents must be suspended from service.
A driver's licence expiry date must be later than its issue date, and an expired licence makes the driver ineligible for trip assignment.
Planning, On Trip, Mandatory Rest, Document Suspension, and Retired driver states must be controlled by operational events rather than manual status changes.
A vehicle that reaches its maintenance threshold must be marked Maintenance Pending when idle or locked for maintenance immediately after its active trip.
Opening maintenance work must place the vehicle in Maintenance; the vehicle may return to Active only when all maintenance work is resolved and its mandatory documents remain valid.
Cold-chain monitoring must be active for trips that are In Transit or Delayed.
A monitoring device that submits a valid reading must be treated as Online and its latest observed condition must be retained for operational monitoring.
A monitoring device with no signal for more than five minutes must be treated as Offline and must have no more than one open Connection Lost alert at a time.
Delivery arrival must be assessed within a 50-metre delivery-point radius, while route deviation must be evaluated against a 1,000-metre warning boundary and a 2,500-metre critical boundary.
After the cargo door is closed at a delivery point, departure from that point must start a 20-minute alert-grace period.
A temperature alert must be raised when monitored cargo exceeds its permitted temperature range.
A temperature risk score of 90 or above must be classified as Critical; a lower confirmed excursion must be classified as High.
Predictive temperature risk must be assessed over a 30-minute forecast horizon.
The standard monitoring profile must be -25°C to -18°C for frozen fruit, meat, and seafood; -25°C to -20°C for ice cream and juice; and 2°C to 8°C for chilled pharmaceuticals and vaccines.
During an approved alert-grace or temperature-mute period, temperature and forecast alerts may be suppressed, but cargo-door alerts must remain active.
Operational cold-chain alerts must be directed to the responsible dispatcher and assigned driver.
A driver may report an incident only for a trip to which the driver is assigned, and the report must identify the incident location and supporting evidence.
A delivery stop affected by a reported incident must enter Delayed by Incident until operational handling is completed.
A driver-paid incident expense greater than zero must enter Pending Approval; an incident without a driver-paid expense requires no reimbursement review.
Additional incident evidence must not be added after the incident is Resolved.
An approved reimbursement must not exceed the amount paid by the driver and must be supported by a reimbursement receipt before it is marked Reimbursed.
An incident may be resolved only with a resolution note and after any approved driver reimbursement has been completed.
A rescue incident may be resolved only after transloading is complete and the trip has continued with the replacement vehicle.
A rescue vehicle must differ from the failed vehicle, be Active, have sufficient weight, volume, and temperature capability for all Shipping LPNs, and have its own monitoring device.

Dispatching a rescue must place the failed vehicle in Maintenance, the replacement vehicle On Trip, the trip in Delayed, and the incident in Rescue Dispatched without changing the trip's commercial identity.
A rescued trip may return to In Transit only after cargo transloading is confirmed and the replacement vehicle's monitoring connection is operational.
A customer claim must be opened with supporting evidence.
A claim that is Resolved or Rejected must not be adjudicated again.
Quality or Dispatch personnel may approve a claim for Accountant Review or reject it; the related order must reflect that decision.
Only Accounting personnel may finalize an approved claim payout.
A successful claim payout must place the claim in Resolved and Paid and must record the corresponding outgoing financial entry.
When an approved loss is assigned to driver debt, the business must create an unpaid driver penalty and mark the order as completed with the approved OSD refund.
A periodic customer invoice may include only completed orders that have an approved quotation and have not already been invoiced.
Periodic invoice charges must comprise approved base freight, last-mile charges, and value-added services, plus 8 percent value-added tax.
A periodic invoice must be issued to the owning customer in Pending status and must be due within 15 days.
Only an assigned driver may check in at a delivery stop, and check-in requires arrival evidence within the approved 200-metre delivery radius.
Delivery may be confirmed or rejected only by an assigned driver after check-in and only for an LPN on the same trip that remains in Shipping.
A delivery decision must identify the receiver and include proof of handover or rejection; bank-transfer payment also requires payment evidence.
The cargo temperature at handover must be recorded from the latest available monitored condition.
A successful handover must place the LPN in Delivered; a rejected handover must place it in Delivery Returned.
A delivery rejection must be classified as Damaged, Wrong Item, Customer Refusal, Temperature Deviation, or Other; an Other rejection requires an explanatory note.

An order may reach its delivery outcome only when no LPN remains in Shipping and no delivered cash-on-delivery amount remains unverified; the outcome must be Delivered, Returned, or Partially Delivered according to its LPN results.
A trip may be completed only when none of its LPNs remains in Shipping.
A delivered cash-on-delivery order must remain in Shipping until the payment is verified; successful verification must finalize the delivery without creating a duplicate payment.
A documented customer no-show must mark the stop Skipped for No-Show, the order Delivery Failed by No-Show, and the affected LPNs Return Pending.
Cutting a trip seal must stop normal cargo monitoring and start a three-hour alert-mute period; applying a replacement seal must restart monitoring with a 15-minute recovery period.
Cash-on-delivery collection may be recorded only after confirmed handover by an assigned driver, and only one collection may be recorded for an order.
A cash collection with evidence must be marked Paid and must complete the incoming payment and proof-of-delivery record.
A QR collection must remain Awaiting Payment until provider confirmation is received and must not finalize proof of delivery until the driver verifies the collection.
A driver may close a delivery shift only after handover has been confirmed for every order on the trip; shift closure must complete the trip and release eligible fleet resources.
